name: ranked-product-list
title: Ranked product list
description: Best sellers as a numbered list: a big rank figure, thumbnail, price, proof and a movement word, with a week, month or all-time switch.
docs: Pass items best first: a product's rank is its place in the array. An item is { id, name, href (the whole row is this link), price in minor units (8900 is 89.00), compareAtPrice?, subtitle?, image? ({ src, alt?, width?, height? }, drawn with renderImage so next/image plugs in), proof? (the line, already written: '1,240 sold this week'), rating?, ratingCount?, movement? and available? }. Movement is { kind: 'new' } | { kind: 'same' } | { kind: 'up' | 'down', by } and is always a word as well as an arrow ('New', 'Up 2', 'Down 1', 'Steady'): under the rank figure on a wide list, under the name on a phone. available false keeps the place but switches Add off and says 'Sold out'; a screen reader hears the product's name with 'is sold out' (soldOutName), so the words it sees are in the name it hears. The list is controlled: you hold period and pass the items for it. periods defaults to This week, This month and All time, and onPeriodChange is called with the value that was chosen (without it the periods are not offered and the list just names the one it shows). A polite status says which period the list shows and how many products. onAddToCart(item) may return a promise: the button shows it is working, says Added with a check and goes back to rest; when the promise rejects the button says Try again for a few seconds and a polite message tells a screen reader that the product could not be added; without it there are no buttons. The button is as wide as its longest word in every state, so the columns of the row never move when it changes. limit shows only the first places, linkAs renders the row links with your router's Link, currency and locale write the prices and numbers, and labels holds the fixed words. On a phone the picture shrinks, the proof moves under the name and the Add button is a square with the plus.
